title: Chapter 85: I Should Be Afraid!
html:
Through the sliver of his open door, Chen Ge watched the red shadow stop before the sixth cubicle. Only a thin partition separated them. As confrontation loomed, time seemed to slow.

Several seconds later, the red shadow leaned toward the door. Chen Ge raised his mallet. The shadow touched the door, and as it creaked open, every muscle in his body tensed.

Before the door opened fully, the red shadow phased through it. Survival instinct took over. Chen Ge brought the mallet down and, in the same motion, kicked the door with all his strength.

Bang!

The decrepit door could not withstand the blow. It tore from its hinges and slammed into the red shadow before it could evade. Its body blurred as it tumbled across the floor, then fled the toilet.

Chen Ge gulped down air. He had expected a fierce battle, but his opponent proved far more timid than anticipated. His sudden attack seemed to have frightened it.

Did that thing forget it’s a ghost?Chen Ge kept a tight grip on the mallet. After the red shadow fled, children’s sobs drifted from the fifth cubicle. The two children he believed belonged to Fan Yu’s aunt were still inside.

“Stop crying!” Sobbing from a toilet cubicle should have been the stuff of horror movies, yet one angry warning from Chen Ge silenced it.

He planted himself in the entrance to the fifth cubicle. The two children covered their mouths with their hands, fear filling their pale faces.

“Why are you two acting like the victims?!”

The confrontation with the red shadow had left Chen Ge’s emotions raw. His raised voice and menacing mallet terrified the children. Clutching hands, they half crawled, half ran from the toilet.

Was I being a bit too harsh there?

The children might well be Fan Yu’s brother and sister. Whether to complete the deep-well mission or investigate his parents’ disappearance, Chen Ge had to follow them. They ran quickly, with Chen Ge close behind, leaving the education block and darting into the neighboring office building.

Chen Ge followed closely behind them. When he got onto the second floor, the two kids suddenly disappeared.

Where did they go?

Unlike the other two buildings, the office block had escaped the fire and remained much cleaner.

Chen Ge opened a door at random and peered inside. The room contained two desks, a bookshelf, and a flowerpot on the windowsill.

They disappeared in the blink of an eye, where could they be hiding?

Farther inside, Chen Ge noticed a faded plaque on the floor. It read ‘Mathematics.’

All of the mathematics classes at Mu Yang High School were held in this one small room?

The answer soon occurred to him. Mu Yang High School had so few students that they could easily fit into one room. Fewer students also meant fewer teachers, so the room probably doubled as the mathematics teacher’s office.

A quick search revealed a rotting schoolbag inside one desk drawer. It was tiny and printed with cartoon characters.

Chen Ge placed it on the table and opened the zipper. There was a cartoon coloring book and a box of crayons inside.

Why would these things be inside the Mathematics teacher’s office?

The contents of the school bag did not seem to be for high school students. Chen Ge surmised that the school bag probably belonged to the Mathematics teacher’s child, and the bag had been left behind for some reason.

When Chen Ge opened the crayon box, he found every color except red and black. Fan Yu immediately came to mind. The coloring book confirmed his suspicion: every page showed the same image, a black house containing two small red figures.

The black house remained constant, but the red figures moved from picture to picture. Chen Ge placed Fan Yu’s recent drawing beside the coloring book and drew a quiet breath. At least his drawing style hasn’t changed after all these years.

The drawings offered valuable clues. The rotting bag and the webs filling the drawer showed it had been hidden there long before Mu Yang High School closed.

Fan Yu had drawn ghosts from a very young age; perhaps his unusual sight was innate. If the black house represented his home, then two ghosts had lived there for years.

Relating it to the aunt’s testimony and what Chen Ge had seen earlier, the two ghosts were most likely the aunt’s children.

After living with him so long, his aunt must know about his special sight.Chen Ge studied the two red-and-black drawings. That’s why she so readily brought him to the Haunted House. She spoils him because she’s pouring the love she had for three children into one boy.

The appearance of Fan Yu’s school bag also told Chen Ge another thing; this room likely belonged to Fan Yu’s father. He was Mu Yang High School’s Mathematics teacher.

From the conversation with Fan Yu’s aunt, Chen Ge knew that Fan Yu’s father had been fired from another school due to drinking. However, Fan Yu’s aunt added that other schools rejected Fan Yu’s father, and he had nowhere else to turn to, which was why he had ended up at Mu Yang High School.

That raised another question. What had Fan Yu’s father done while drunk to be blacklisted throughout the district and rejected by every ordinary school?

Chen Ge had wanted to ask, but Fan Yu’s aunt had quickly diverted the conversation by producing the mysterious photograph.

What kind of person was the missing father like?Chen Ge drummed the mallet on the table in thought. He continued to look through the room and finally found several paper notes inside an abandoned book on the bookshelf.

“Teacher Fan, we know what you did in the sixth cubicle of the third floor’s female toilets. We demand that you apologize to the girl immediately! And get out of this school!”

“You have two nights to come to a decision. We want an open apology!”

“This is your last night. If you insist on staying at this school, then you shall stay here forever.”
